restrictions: Messages are exactly 64 bytes: one unkeyed BLAKE3 chunk/block with flags CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT=11, length 64, counter 0, standard IV.

Deterministic closed-form construction from public IV constants; no search, no random coins, no stored precomputed collision as advice; the constant table holds only IV[0..7] and F as nine narrow words (no pre-packed lane vectors).

Columns: every column G0..G3 uses the same identity (Lemma 5, (C*,D*)=(0,-b)), so all four output B=C=0 and D=-b. Diagonals G4/G6 then see b=c=0, d=-IV7/-IV5; M uses x=d-a, y=-d (=IV7, IV5), and M' replaces only w9, w13 by ~d (Lemma 6'), making both diagonals output all-F so the feed-forward pairs (v0,v8),(v2,v10),(v5,v13),(v7,v15) cancel. No IV parity condition is required. Message pair and certificate are bit-identical to the previous 1.77 package.

Implementation: the four columns run in parallel as 32-bit value fields at bit offsets (0,64,160,224) of a 256-bit word; lanes 0-2 have guard gaps, lane 3 is the top 32 bits of the word (no gap, no guard; arithmetic mod 2^256 reduces it mod 2^32 and SHR 224 is always a clean 32-bit word: Lemma S4). Only 256-bit ADD/SUB/AND/OR/XOR/SHL/SHR are used; lane masks, guards, IV packing and lane extraction are all charged. No rotate instruction of any width is used.

The column x/y vectors and the diagonal x vector are only unpacked, so they are extracted directly from the raw guarded differences (Lemma S5): lanes 0-2 by SHR+AND F, lane 3 by SHR 224. A vector AND M before that extraction changes no stored bit for any input (dead code); removing it is the whole -3 ALU vs the 1.77 package. Every vector that feeds further ADD/SUB/XOR or a rotation is still AND M clean (no chaining) and every rotation keeps its final AND (no elision).

Charged work: straight-line program, two verification compressions (H=2), 8x32-bit digest equality and message-distinctness checks, program placement (1 op/instruction) and constant-table placement (2 ops/word), under collision-frontier-v5 with C=222. Ledger W = 2(LD+ALU+ST+V) + 2LD with V=37. Primary stream (LD=9, ALU=60, 18 shared-buffer stores): W=266. Harshest stress row (LD=11, masked-SUB flip ALU=61, 32 stores): W=304.

Claimed scalar time_log2=1.76 (2^1.76~3.3870) covers every row of the ST x LD x flip stress lattice: ceiling W <= (2^1.76-2)*222 ~ 307.91 with H=2; harshest W=304 (T~3.369, log2~1.7525). Claim 1.75 is not made: ceiling ~302.72 < 304; the only -1 candidates found (unmasked S into SUB, guard-absorbs-carry, chained guarded SUB, unmasked sub1 flip) are refused as chaining / mask elision / lattice shopping (proof.md section 6.4-6.5).

Degradation with the same messages (proof.md 6.6, 6.8, Appendix B): 2-way top-lane SWAR harshest W=322 (fits 1.79); serial top-field scalars harshest W=350 (fits 1.84); serial low-limb W=356. The 1.76 resource claim depends on defended 4-wide word-RAM lane packing.

No omit-verify, memory-only placement, native narrow rotate, native 256-bit ROT, packed-IV, pre-packed table vectors, packed-store, packed-EQ, chaining, rotation-AND elision, or BSS reading is used. Certificate blake3-r1-swar-lemma5-pair is an organizer-verifiable witness of the same construction instance; it is not nonuniform advice and does not replace charged collision checking. The proof.md Appendix A emulator executes the exact program and reproduces the instance and every lattice row.

Claim is specific to 1 prefix round; the diagonal cancellation uses the B/C-vanishing column state and does not transfer to 2+ rounds without a new argument. The nominal reference identifier does not itself assert an improvement.
